newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-Boeing, McDonnell problems under-rated - EU.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Boeing, McDonnell problems under-rated - EU.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Monday he might have underestimated the problems with the planned merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
The European Commission would open a full probe later this week, he said.
"There is going to be a fully-fledged investigation," Van Miert told Reuters as he arrived at the European Parliament to speak to a committee on an unrelated subject.
He added: "I have the impression that I had under-rated the problems."
Van Miert declined to detail his competition concerns but a Commission source said the EU would in particular be scrutinising the alliance's impact on the markets for civil aircraft and helicopters.

The Commission is particularly worried about Boeing's dominance of the large-aircraft segment with its 747 jumbo, the source said. Before the alliance, McDonnell was considering developing a high-capacity plane of its own to compete with Boeing.

The source, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said the Commission's preliminary review of the deal -- in which Boeing will take over McDonnell -- contrasted with the U.S. giant's opinion that it did not much change the current market situation.

Boeing has about 60 percent of the world's civil aviation market against 35 percent for the European Airbus consortium between France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace , Spain's CASA and Daimler-Benz of Germany. McDonnell is active mainly in the defence and space industries.
Boeing's chairman and chief executive officer Phil Condit said last week that neither Boeing nor Airbus thought their market share would change much as a result of the alliance.
Airbus has plans to launch its own jumbo jet called A-3XX but it meets funding problems.
The Commission's official announcement of the probe is expected on Wednesday. It could take up to four months.

The merger between the two U.S. aircraft makers was submitted to the EU for clearance last month under EU rules which ban creation or strengthening of dominant positions in the 15-nation bloc. It is also being investigated by the U.S. authorities.
Boeing hopes to have cleared all regulatory hurdles by July. The deal is said to have the backing of the Pentagon.

Van Miert said in reply to a question he was aware of the transatlantic political problems that a tough EU stance on the deal could cause. But this would not prevent the Commission from doing its job, he said.
"It's not because a case may trigger problems with a third country, be it the U.S., that we should refrain from investigating," he said.
He said the Commission was in close contact with the U.S. anti-trust authorities and that it would keep them informed of any problems it detected. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
